_comment: LinkedIn ships fully hashed/atomized CSS class names on this view (e.g. 'aa26e2c6', '_4946ed03') with zero semantic meaning — not just churn-prone, but useless for selectors entirely. Title/company are resolved primarily from document.title (see parseFromDocumentTitle in linkedin.ts); these selectors are a last-resort fallback. Prefer aria-label / attribute-based selectors (href*='/company/') over class names, which can change on every deploy.
_jobDescriptionComment: Verified live 2026-07-12. LinkedIn's job description lives under a container whose 'componentkey' attribute is semantic and stable ('JobDetails_AboutTheJob_{jobId}' — only the numeric jobId suffix changes), unlike the fully hashed CSS classes elsewhere on this view. The actual text sits inside a nested '[data-testid="expandable-text-box"]' span — but that data-testid is NOT unique by itself, since LinkedIn reuses it for the 'About the company'/'Commitments' blurbs too. It must stay scoped under the JobDetails_AboutTheJob container. The older '#job-details'/'.jobs-description__content' guesses never matched and are kept only as a last-resort fallback.
_locationModalityComment: VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-13 against a real authenticated session, both the standalone /jobs/view/ page and the /jobs/search-results/ split pane. Location verified on multiple postings; modality verified on a real 'On-site' pill and a real 'Remote' pill (checked a job under LinkedIn's Hybrid filter too, but that specific posting's own pill happened to read 'Remote' — no literal 'Hybrid' pill was observed, though the code path is identical for all three values). Like title/company, there is NO stable selector reachable here at all — every element up the tree from the location text is fully hashed with no data-testid/componentkey (confirmed by walking the DOM by hand), so this can't be expressed as a plain selectors array the way other platforms are. Location and modality are instead resolved in code (see resolveLocationAndModality() in linkedin.ts) by walking up from the stable company-profile link (companySelectors' 'a[href*="/company/"]') to the nearby bullet-separated metadata line ('{location} · {posted} · {applicants}') and, a couple of levels further out, an exact-text workplace-type pill ('Remote'/'Hybrid'/'On-site') — guarded with both a `.closest('nav')` exclusion (the search-results filter sidebar reuses the exact same words as its own filter-chip labels) and a distinct-company-profile-link bound on the widening scope (stops before the scope could span into a sibling job card's own metadata on the split-pane view — a single job card can legitimately have a second bullet-separated line of its own, e.g. 'Promoted by hirer · Responses managed off LinkedIn', so bounding on company links rather than bullet-line count was necessary; verified live against both failure modes). Hrefs are compared by pathname only (stripping query string) before dedup, since a company's logo-anchor and text-anchor can carry different tracking parameters on an otherwise-identical link, which would otherwise make one job's own card look like two companies. modalityTextMatches below is still used by that function's detectModality() call.
